items.en: Is Dharma Contaminated, or Mind, or Neither Alone?
items.zh: 料簡法心 · 四句推檢
parent: V. Discriminating the Dharma and Mind of Dhyāna-Pāramitā

zh: 問曰：此四種法心，法之與心，有何等異？如有漏法有漏心，此法心為當各是有漏，為當各非？故說漏若二各有者，法心合時應有二漏法起；若各無，和合亦應無。答曰：今不得言二各是漏，亦不得言二法中各都無漏。何以故？若心即是漏，如阿羅漢漏盡時，心應盡，法亦如是。所以者何？若法定是漏者，聖人入根本四禪亦應生漏。此四禪法未與心合，亦應自是漏。而聖人入四禪法不生於漏，四禪法未與心相應時，亦自無有漏法生，云何言法即是有漏？今言此漏不獨在法，亦不獨在心，法心合時便有漏生。以有有漏故，二處受名。譬如仙藥，人若服之，即令得仙。而藥之與人，本各非仙，藥人和合，則便有仙。故藥受仙藥之名，人受仙人之稱。若藥不因人，不名仙藥；人不因藥，不名仙人。漏法、漏心亦復如是。
en: Question: Among these four kinds of dharma-mind, what is the actual difference between dharma and mind? Take contaminated dharma and contaminated mind: are these each, individually, contaminated, or are they not? For if it is said that the contaminant belongs to each of the two separately, then when dharma and mind come together, two separate contaminated dharmas ought to arise; and if it belongs to neither separately, their union ought likewise to produce nothing.

Answer: One cannot say that both, taken separately, are contaminated, nor can one say that neither, taken separately, is contaminated at all. Why is this? If mind itself simply were the contaminant, then at the moment an arhat's contaminants are exhausted, the mind itself ought to be exhausted. The same holds for dharma. Why is this? If dharma were fixed as being, in itself, the contaminant, then a noble one entering the root four dhyānas ought also to give rise to the contaminant — since these four dhyāna-dharmas, prior to ever joining with mind, ought already to be contaminated in themselves. Yet a noble one entering the four dhyānas does not give rise to the contaminant at all; before the dharma of the four dhyānas has even come into accord with mind, no contaminated dharma arises there either — how, then, could dharma itself simply be the contaminant?

Here it is said that this contaminant belongs neither to dharma alone nor to mind alone — it is only when dharma and mind come together that the contaminant arises. And because there is a contaminant, both are given their respective names. It is like an elixir of immortality: when a person takes it, it grants them immortality — yet the elixir, and the person, are each, in themselves, neither one immortal. Only when elixir and person come together is there immortality at all. Hence the elixir receives the name "elixir of immortality," and the person receives the title "immortal." If the elixir did not depend on the person, it would not be called the elixir of immortality; if the person did not depend on the elixir, they would not be called an immortal. The contaminated dharma and the contaminated mind are exactly the same.

zh:
餘三種法心義類爾可知，故阿難說示比丘為舍利弗說偈：
諸法從緣生，是法說因緣，
是法緣及盡，我師如是說。
復次，若謂有漏之法，自有有漏法；若有漏之法由有漏心故，有有漏法；若有漏法由法由心故，有有漏法；若有漏之法不由法不由心故，有有漏法。如此之計，皆墮邪見。所以者何？若謂由有漏法故，有有漏法者，即是自性有漏法。若是自性有漏法，則應有無窮之漏法，以自性復有自性故。今實不爾。若謂有漏法不能自有，由有漏心故有者，即是他性有漏法。所以者何？若有漏法待有漏心為自性者，今有漏心待有漏法，豈非他性？若由他性而有有漏法者，他性若是有有漏法，則有漏法還是有漏法，更無心法之別；他性若非有漏法，非有漏法何能有有漏法？故知有漏法不由有漏心故有。若謂有漏法由有漏法、有漏心故有者，即是共有。若是共有，則從自、他性中而有有漏法。若爾，則一時應有二有漏法。今實不然，故知非自、他、共故有有漏法。若謂離有漏法，離有漏心，有有漏法者，即是無因緣而有有漏法。從因緣有有漏法尚不可，何況無因緣而有有漏法？破因成假，廣說如《止觀》。有漏心亦如是，餘三種法心亦如是。
en:
The remaining three kinds of dharma-mind may be understood along the same lines. Hence the bhikṣu Aśvajit spoke this verse for Śāriputra [the text here reads 阿難說示比丘, "Ānanda… the bhikṣu shuoshi"; other sūtras give 阿說示比丘, the bhikṣu Aśvajit, from whom Śāriputra first heard this verse, and the 難 is likely an error]:
"All dharmas arise from conditions;
This dharma is spoken of as cause and condition;
This dharma has both its conditions and their extinction —
Thus has my Teacher taught."

Furthermore: suppose one holds that contaminated dharma has, of itself, contaminated dharma; or that contaminated dharma exists because of contaminated mind; or that contaminated dharma exists because of both dharma and mind together; or that contaminated dharma exists apart from both dharma and mind. Every such supposition falls into wrong view. Why is this?

If it is held that contaminated dharma exists because of contaminated dharma itself, this is "contaminated dharma from self-nature." But if it were contaminated dharma from self-nature, then there would have to be a contaminated dharma without end, since a self-nature would itself have to have a further self-nature behind it — and this is, in fact, not so.

If it is held that contaminated dharma cannot exist of itself, but exists because of contaminated mind, this is "contaminated dharma from another's nature." But why is this? If contaminated dharma depends on contaminated mind as its own nature, then contaminated mind, in turn, depends on contaminated dharma — how, then, is this not equally "another's nature"? And if contaminated dharma exists because of another's nature: if that other nature is itself already contaminated dharma, then contaminated dharma is still simply contaminated dharma, with no distinction from mind-dharma left at all; and if that other nature is not contaminated dharma, how could what is not contaminated dharma give rise to contaminated dharma? Hence it is known that contaminated dharma does not exist because of contaminated mind.

If it is held that contaminated dharma exists because of contaminated dharma and contaminated mind together, this is "joint existence." But if it is joint existence, then contaminated dharma would have to exist out of both self-nature and another's nature at once — and if so, there ought to be two contaminated dharmas arising at the same time. This, too, is in fact not so. Hence it is known that contaminated dharma does not exist through self-nature, another's nature, or their joint action.

If it is held that contaminated dharma exists apart from both contaminated dharma and contaminated mind, this is contaminated dharma existing without any cause or condition at all. If contaminated dharma existing through causes and conditions is already untenable, how much more untenable is contaminated dharma existing without any cause or condition whatsoever? Refuting the provisional reality established by cause is explained fully in the Great Calming and Contemplation. Contaminated mind is exactly the same, and the remaining three kinds of dharma-mind are likewise the same.

zh: 復次，若有漏法定是有漏法者，是有漏法即是生滅相續法，為生故生，為滅故生，為生滅故生，為離生離滅得生？若是生生，即是自生；若由滅故生，即是他生；若由生滅故生，即共生。若離生滅而說生者，即是無因緣生。從因緣生尚不可，何況無因緣生？當知有漏生畢竟不可得。若無生則無滅，若無生滅即無相續，若無生滅相續，則無有漏法。破相續假，廣說如《止觀》。有漏心亦如是，餘三種法心亦如是。復次，若有漏法是生者，為生生故生，為不生生故生，為生不生故生，為非生非不生故生？若生生，則是自性生；若不生生，即是他性生；若生不生故生，即是共生；若非生非不生故生，即是無因緣生。從因緣生尚不可，何況無因緣生？是則於相待假中求有漏法生畢竟不可得。若無生，則無有漏。破相待假，廣說如《止觀》。有漏心亦如是，餘三種法心亦如是。當知有漏之法於因成、相續、相待中各各四句求畢竟不可得。若不可得，云何分別有有漏法？若無有有漏之法而說有漏法者，當知但有名字，是中不應定有所依，生諸戲論，破智慧眼。次明有漏心亦如是，若有漏法心如是，餘三句法心亦如是，但以世間名字故，說名字之法不在內、外、兩中間，亦不常，自有無名之名，故曰假名。
en: Furthermore: if contaminated dharma were fixed as, definitely, contaminated dharma, then this contaminated dharma would be a dharma of arising, ceasing, and continuing on — does it arise because of arising, because of ceasing, because of both arising and ceasing, or by leaving both arising and ceasing behind? If it arises by way of arising, this is self-arising; if it arises because of ceasing, this is other-arising; if it arises because of both arising and ceasing, this is joint arising; and if arising is spoken of apart from both arising and ceasing, this is arising without any cause or condition. If arising through causes and conditions is already untenable, how much more untenable is arising without any cause or condition? One should know, then, that the arising of the contaminated can, in the end, never be found. If there is no arising, there is no ceasing; if there is no arising and ceasing, there is no continuity; and if there is no continuity of arising and ceasing, then there is no contaminated dharma at all. Refuting the provisional reality established by continuity is explained fully in the Great Calming and Contemplation. Contaminated mind is exactly the same, and the remaining three kinds of dharma-mind are likewise the same.

Furthermore: if contaminated dharma is something that arises, does it arise because of arising, because of not-arising, because of both arising and not-arising, or because of neither arising nor not-arising? If it arises through arising, this is arising from self-nature; if it arises through not-arising, this is arising from another's nature; if it arises because of both arising and not-arising, this is joint arising; and if it arises because of neither arising nor not-arising, this is arising without any cause or condition. If arising through causes and conditions is already untenable, how much more untenable is arising without any cause or condition? Hence, seeking the arising of contaminated dharma within the provisional reality established by mutual dependence, it can, in the end, never be found. If there is no arising, there is no contaminated dharma. Refuting the provisional reality established by mutual dependence is explained fully in the Great Calming and Contemplation. Contaminated mind is exactly the same, and the remaining three kinds of dharma-mind are likewise the same.

One should know, then, that contaminated dharma, sought through this same fourfold scheme within each of the three provisional realities — establishment by cause, continuity, and mutual dependence alike — can, in the end, never be found. If it can never be found, how can a contaminated dharma be distinguished as existing at all? And if there is, in truth, no contaminated dharma, yet contaminated dharma is still spoken of — one should know that this is merely a matter of names, and that no fixed basis should be assumed to underlie it, lest idle theorizing be produced and the eye of wisdom destroyed. Contaminated mind, next, should be understood in exactly the same way. If contaminated dharma-mind is thus, the remaining three kinds of dharma-mind are likewise thus — it is only in terms of worldly names that this dharma of naming is spoken of; it is not located inside, outside, or in between the two, nor is it permanent; it possesses, of itself, a name that is really no name at all — hence it is called a "provisional name."

zh: 問曰：若爾，云何分別法心之異？答曰：但以世間名字故，分別法心之別，是中無有定實。問曰：云何於名字中分別法心之別？答曰：若知法心無所有，但有名字，則還如上分別法心之相無咎。故《大品經》云：「須菩提！不壞假名而說諸法實相。」復次，如心數為法，心王為心。受、想、行三陰及色陰為法，識陰為心。心相應法、心不相應法及色法、無為法為法，心法為心。所緣為法，能緣為心。能生為法，所生為心。所觀之境為法，能觀之智為心。法成於心，心依於法。如是等，於名字中種種分別法、心之別。雖作此分別，皆如幻化，無所取著，同歸一相。此義至下第十、結會歸趣中當廣釋。
en: Question: If this is so, how can the difference between dharma and mind be distinguished at all? Answer: It is only in terms of worldly names that the difference between dharma and mind is distinguished — there is nothing fixed or truly real underlying it. Question: How, then, is the difference between dharma and mind distinguished within mere names? Answer: If one knows that dharma and mind possess nothing at all, and are only names, then distinguishing the mark of dharma and mind as above involves no fault. Hence the Larger Sūtra says: "Subhūti! Without destroying the provisional name, the true reality of all dharmas is spoken of."

Furthermore: the mental factors are dharma, the ruling mind is mind. The three aggregates of sensation, perception, and formations, together with the aggregate of form, are dharma; the aggregate of consciousness is mind. Mind-associated dharmas, mind-dissociated dharmas, form-dharmas, and unconditioned dharmas are dharma; mind-dharma itself is mind. What is taken as an object is dharma; what takes an object is mind. What generates is dharma; what is generated is mind. The object contemplated is dharma; the wisdom that contemplates is mind. Dharma is accomplished through mind, and mind depends upon dharma. In ways such as these, the difference between dharma and mind is variously distinguished within mere names. Though these distinctions are made, they are, every one, like a magical illusion — nothing to be grasped at or clung to, all alike returning to a single mark. This point will be explained fully further below, in the tenth topic, where the treatise is gathered together and its destination pointed out.

This closing stretch runs the "contaminated" through Nāgārjuna's classic fourfold refutation of causation three separate times — first asking whether contaminated dharma is produced by itself, by mind, by both, or by neither (refuting "establishment by cause," 因成假); then whether it arises through arising, ceasing, both, or neither, so that with no arising there is no ceasing and no continuity (refuting "continuity," 相續假); and finally whether it arises through arising, not-arising, both, or neither (refuting "mutual dependence," 相待假). Each of the "three provisional realities" (因成假, 相續假, 相待假) is a distinct Tiantai lens for how something can seem to exist conventionally while having no fixed essence under any of the four alternatives — full treatment is deferred here to the Great Calming and Contemplation (《止觀》, i.e. the Mohe Zhiguan), a separate, much longer work of Zhiyi's, also translated on this site.

The elixir-and-immortal analogy is worth remembering on its own: it is Zhiyi's answer to a puzzle that recurs constantly in Buddhist philosophy — how two things that are each, on their own, "neither this quality nor that," can combine to produce something with a real, functioning quality neither one possessed alone. The upshot for practice: dharma and mind, contamination and purity, are none of them free-standing, self-sufficient properties waiting to be found — they arise, and are named, only in relation. This closes topic 5, and with it, the whole of fascicle 1.

quiz.q: The text says contamination belongs neither to dharma alone nor to mind alone, but arises when they meet. What simile does it use?
options: a cart-wheel strong on one side
the elixir: neither elixir nor person is immortal in itself, but together there is immortality
quiz.why: "It is like an elixir of immortality ... yet the elixir, and the person, are each, in themselves, neither one immortal. Only when elixir and person come together is there immortality at all ... The contaminated dharma and the contaminated mind are exactly the same." Empty space is the earlier image showing that ungraspable emptiness does not obstruct speaking of the fourfold scheme.

quiz.q: In which three kinds of provisional reality does the text seek contaminated dharma through the fourfold examination and find it can never be found?
options: establishment by cause, continuity, mutual dependence
quiz.why: "Contaminated dharma, sought through this same fourfold scheme within each of the three provisional realities — establishment by cause, continuity, and mutual dependence alike — can, in the end, never be found." Self, other, joint, and causeless are the four alternatives within each; worldly and the rest are siddhāntas.
